Q: Thanks for taking the time to speak with me today. This recorded statement is about the collision you reported in
Houston. Do you understand that this call is being recorded?
A: Yes, I understand.
Q: Please tell me in your own words what happened.
A: I was driving down the main road in the right lane. The other car came over into my lane while trying to pass a
slower vehicle. I tapped the brakes and steered right, but we still met nose to nose. It wasn't a hard hit, but it was
enough to jolt me.
Q: How fast were you going when the vehicles made contact?
A: I'd say maybe fifteen or twenty miles an hour. Traffic was moving slowly that afternoon.
Q: Were you wearing your seatbelt?
A: Yes, I was. The airbags didn't deploy, but the belt caught me hard.
Q: Did you get checked out by anyone after the collision?
A: I drove myself to an urgent care clinic later that evening. My neck was sore and stiff, and I had a headache that got
worse overnight.
Q: Can you describe the neck symptoms you are experiencing now?
A: It's tight across the back and sides, and turning my head to the left hurts. Sitting at a desk for long stretches makes
it worse. The doctor said it looks like a neck strain and gave me exercises and some medication.
Q: Have you had any neck problems or injuries before this collision?
A: Nothing serious. I had some stiffness now and then from sleeping wrong, but nothing that kept me from working.
Q: Is there anything else you would like to add to your statement?
A: No, I think that covers it. I'm still going to physical therapy twice a week, and I'll send you the records when I get
them.
Q: Thank you. This concludes the statement.
</page>

injury. Do not list the date of a note, letter, report, visit, statement, filing or signature.

it is the loss date. Examples: "Date of loss:", "Crash date:", "Date of injury:", "the collision on".
